text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- Syrian President Assad to Israel: Syria interested in reaching peace agreement within months.
- U.S. administration studying proposal to settle Palestinian refugees in all Middle Eastern countries including Israel.
- Housing Ministry preparing to market land for construction of 4,550 housing units in the West Bank in 1997.
- Senior Bank of Israel officials say further 1.3 billion shekel budget cut needed.
- Maof index hits record high.
- Bank Hapoalim forecasts no great rush for foreign currency in 1997.
- January tax revenues 500 million shekels below budget forecast.
- George Soros plans to boost his Israeli investments.
- Finance Minister Meridor asks parliament's finance committee to approve sale of 17 percent stake in Israel Discount Bank within two weeks.
- Parliament's finance committee to approve today continued privatisation of Israel Chemicals.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Peace treaty with Syria was supposed to have been signed in October 1996.
MAARIV
- Tel Aviv stock market returns to record levels.
- Finance Minister Meridor and Bank of Israel Governor Frenkel to meet today to try to bridge differences over exchange rate.
- Heineken and Tempo in $43 million partnership deal.
- Bank of Israel considering 15 percent surcharge on short-term foreign currency loans.
GLOBES
- Israeli shares rise three percent, Maof hits record high.
- Netanyahu fails in Davos to reach agreement with his finance minister and governor of Bank of Israel on foreign exchange and interest rates.
JERUSALEM POST
- Pope wants to visit before 2000.
- U.S. official says Israel should stay in Lebanon.
- Palestinian Authority: Prisoner killers will be prosecuted.
- Israeli army opens part of Hebron's Shuhada Street to Palestinians.
